name: Raene's Cleansing
summary: This critical stage of Raene Wolfrunner's mission requires the use of Dartol's newly restored rod to disguise an outsider and initiate contact with an uncorrupted furbolg. Southeast of Mystral Lake, an outcast named Krolg offers a rare glimpse into the surviving furbolgs' deep resentment toward the night elves.

sections.title: A Guise of Fur and Claw
sections.body: With Dartol's Rod of Transformation restored, Raene Wolfrunner suspects the late night elf intended to disguise himself in order to safely approach the furbolgs. The woods of Ashenvale have grown perilous, and the madness spreading through the tribes makes direct diplomacy impossible. By harnessing the arcane relic, an adventurer takes on the appearance of a furbolg, hoping to slip past instinctive territorial rage and find someone willing to speak.

sections.title: The Exile's Bitterness
sections.body: Southeast of Mystral Lake lies Krolg, an isolated furbolg who has managed to escape the corrupting touch of Fel Moss. Believing he is speaking to a clean member of his own kin, Krolg speaks freely of his exile and profound sorrow. Yet rather than seeing the night elves as allies or protectors, he harbors deep bitterness toward them, openly blaming night elven hubris and ancient failures for the demonic taint ravaging his people.

faq.q: What does Dartol's Rod of Transformation do?
faq.answer: Dartol's Rod of Transformation temporarily changes the bearer's appearance into that of a furbolg. This disguise allows an adventurer to walk among uncorrupted furbolgs without inciting an immediate violent attack.

Krolg is an uncorrupted furbolg living in exile southeast of Mystral Lake. Having avoided the Fel Moss that infected his kin, he lives alone across a torch-lined stream, mourning the loss of his tribe while holding a deep grudge against night elf kind.

faq.q: Why will Krolg attack if you don't use the rod?
aliases: why use the rod on krolg
faq.answer: Krolg is terrified and deeply distrustful of outsiders, particularly the night elves whom he blames for his people's downfall. Without the illusion making you look like an uncorrupted furbolg, he will treat you as an intruder and defend his camp violently.

faq.q: Why does Krolg blame the night elves for the corruption?
aliases: why does krolg hate night elves
faq.answer: Krolg views the demonic corruption of the forest—brought on by the Legion's invasions and historical arcane meddling—as the direct fault of night elven pride. In his eyes, the ancient Kaldorei brought ruin upon Kalimdor and left the indigenous tribes to suffer the consequences.
He can be found southeast of Mystral Lake in Ashenvale. Follow a winding dirt path marked by burning torches that leads down across a small stream to his solitary camp.

faq.q: What is Fel Moss and how did it affect the furbolgs?
faq.answer: Fel Moss is a demonic growth spreading through Ashenvale that seeps demonic taint into the soil and flora. The local furbolg tribes fell victim to its influence, driving them into a state of rabid, violent insanity that fractured their society.

angles.text: Hearing Krolg's words is a sobering reminder that many indigenous denizens of Ashenvale do not view the Kaldorei as benevolent guardians, but as the reckless architects of the land's recurring doom.
Druids seeking to restore balance to the forest are confronted with the raw tragedy of the furbolgs, who were once close nature allies but now suffer horrific madness from lingering demonic filth.
Astranaar's survival depends on unraveling the threats lurking along the border roads, making this covert parley essential for securing eastern Ashenvale.
